stanza: a cramped one-room home of a poor family in a remote mountain village, present day, late afternoon: plain painted walls with a few damp stains and nothing hanging on them except a small wooden crucifix; on the left an old black cast-iron wood stove, cold, with its small front door ajar and a folded white cloth stuffed inside instead of firewood; next to it a tiny kitchen corner with a chipped enamel sink and a two-burner gas cooker; on the right an unmade double bed with an iron headboard, a thin mattress and a crumpled brown blanket, and next to the bed a worn brown armchair with a small table beside it holding an old nebulizer machine; at the back a window with half-closed plastic roller blinds. A ceiling lamp gives even light.
persone: Two people face the viewer in tense silence. In the middle of the room stands the wife, a short, broad and sturdy woman in her fifties, healthy and solid, with her arms crossed: a big round head with a high bulging forehead, small dark eyes set wide apart under thick straight black eyebrows, a small flat nose, a wide thin mouth pressed shut, and jet-black hair cut in a severe blunt bob with a straight fringe; she wears a clean, buttoned dark green cardigan with a high collar over a dark grey dress, thick tights and black work shoes. On the right, in the worn armchair next to the bed, sits her husband, a huge, heavy, barrel-chested retired quarryman in his seventies, big and strong rather than thin: an enormous smooth bald head, large ears, heavy brows over small pale eyes, a broad flat nose, a thick white walrus moustache and enormous hands resting on his knees; he wears a white vest and a brown wool blanket over his shoulders and legs, the plastic mask of a nebulizer hanging on his chest. They are hiding something, and their faces show it: she glares, he stares without blinking.
pose: the woman standing in the middle with her arms crossed and the man sitting in the armchair wrapped in the blanket
oggetti: the cold wood stove with its door ajar and the white cloth inside, the sink and the gas cooker, the unmade double bed, the armchair, the small table with the nebulizer, the window with the half-closed blinds and the crucifix
tratti: strange caricatures rather than sick ones: exaggerated and distorted proportions, oversized and oddly shaped heads, eyes too big, too small or set too far apart, odd noses, long necks, big or long hands; their mouths closed, with the same tense, serious expressions as in the photo: no smiles, no grins, no visible teeth; unsettling and sinister, but healthy and well fed, with full cheeks and clean skin: never sick, wasted, dirty or dying, never cute or cartoonish
tratti_foto: the same oversized, oddly shaped heads, the same strange eyes and noses, the same closed mouths and serious expressions, the same long necks and big or long hands, with healthy skin and full cheeks; the woman is in her fifties, with smooth, firm skin and only a few fine lines, the man in his seventies, big and strong (the hatching of the drawing is shading, not wrinkles)
